compiled_state.title: As a DSO reviewer agent, I emit verification_evidence on every finding that makes an absence claim
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Update all 10 existing `code-reviewer-*` agent files to emit `verification_evidence: {command, output}` on every finding that makes an absence claim. Each agent must run a grep/stat/path-resolve command and capture its output as proof.

**Why**: The verifier agent (S3) needs the evidence payload to confirm or refute absence claims. Without it, the verifier has no evidentiary anchor and must fall back to fail-open (confirm).

**Scope**:
- IN: Updating prompt files for all 10 agents (light, standard, performance, deep-arch, deep-correctness, deep-hygiene, deep-verification, security-red-team, security-blue-team, test-quality); behavioral fixture per agent asserting emission on a known absence-claim diff
- OUT: Schema validation enforcement (S1), verifier agent (S3), dispatch wiring (S4, S5)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, all 10 `code-reviewer-*` agent files emit `verification_evidence: {command: string, output: string}` on findings citing absence-language matching the canonical + expanded synonym anchor list defined in S1
  ← Satisfies: "All 10 existing code-reviewer-* agent files updated to emit verification_evidence when their finding cites absence-language; each agent has a behavioral fixture asserting it emits the field on a known absence-claim diff"
- When this story is complete, each of the 10 agents has a behavioral fixture using a distinct test diff (not shared across agents) that asserts the field is emitted; fixtures run in soft-deprecation mode per the S1 version-marker contract
  ← Satisfies: "The 10 agents are updated in a single plugin-cache version bump alongside the schema validator"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Testing] Each of the 10 agents needs a distinct test diff — avoid sharing fixtures across agents to prevent false positives masking per-agent regression

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
